key_insight: Yield stress suppresses Taylor dispersion under fixed pressure and electrical forcing but increases it at fixed mean throughput in Casson microflows.
engineering_relevance: Predicting tracer spreading in yield-stress microfluidics requires accounting for whether pressure or throughput is controlled.
method: Solve nonlinear Casson stress and velocity equations for yielded layers and the unyielded core.
Apply multiple-scale homogenization to derive effective longitudinal diffusivity.
Use an energy identity to connect dispersion to velocity departures from the sectional mean.
evidence_signal: Analytical limits, direct concentration calculations and convergence tests support predictions: raising Y from 0 to 0.7 lowers optimum normalized diffusivity from 1.454 to 1.015 under fixed forcing, but raises it from 1.000433 to 1.002311 at fixed throughput and Ha_p = 1.
watch_item: The magnetic optima are theoretical forcing states for representative aqueous microchannels; practical magnetic-field feasibility needs assessment.
paper_title: Yielding-dependent Taylor dispersion in electrokinetic-magnetohydrodynamic Casson microflows
